newsitem.title: UK: Aluminium firms from 2-1/2 year lows on Russia talk.
newsitem.headline: Aluminium firms from 2-1/2 year lows on Russia talk.

text.p: Aluminium prices picked themselves up off 2-1/2 year lows on Friday on the London Metal Exchange (LME) as news emerged that some Russian smelters were considering cutting production, traders said.
LME three months aluminium ended at $1,337 a tonne, not much different from the Thursday close but firmer than they were just before the news and somewhat above a low at $1,305 hit during Thursday.
In Moscow, Oleg Deripaska, chief executive officer of Sayansk Aluminium said he expected a decision to decrease production at Russia's Bratsk, Sayansk and Krasnoyarsk smelters after producers meet.

Western experts and officials adopted a wait-and-see attitude to the possible development. Canada said no new Memorandum of Understanding on output curbs by big world producing nations was being planned. LME coppered to break above resistance at $1,970 per tonne despite an unusually big draw on LME stocks in the latest week of 18,450 tonnes.

Copper, on a rebound, had flirted with $1,970 in late Thursday inter-office activity but could not breach it. Right after the stocks data on Friday it held just above that threshold but was not very busy.
This suggested that the market had factored in a big decline in stocks as the price ran up earlier in the week.

Copper eventually ended Friday down $1 on the day at $1,957. Precious metals prices also drifted lower on Friday reflecting a lack of followthrough buying after silver led the complex higher on Thursday.
Gold closed at $381.35 per ounce after Thursday's $381.95.
Crude oil was just firmer while Chicago wheat futures and London coffee, cocoa and sugar ended little changed.
But Chicago Board of Trade soybean futures dropped nearly the 30 cent per bushel limit on a higher government estimate for 1996 U.S. soybean production.
"The numbers set the tone for the market today and beans are acting like they should, there are too many beans," said Steve Bruce of E.D. and F. Man International.
USDA early Friday said 1996 US soybean production would total 2.346 billion bushels. The average trade estimate was for 2.287 billion.
The January soybean contract was down 25 cents at $7.12 by mid-session in Chicago.
